bug_semantics: An authenticated remote caller controls baseUrl in POST /api/provider-nodes/validate. The route passes baseUrl-derived URLs to server-side fetches and forwards the caller's apiKey as Authorization credentials. assertPublicUrl parses the URL, but its IPv4-mapped IPv6 check expects a dotted quad after ::ffff:, whereas WHATWG URL parsing canonicalizes that input to hexadecimal hextets first. Thus mapped loopback and link-local literals such as http://[::ffff:7f00:1] and http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe] pass the guard and reach internal services. The custom-embedding path reflects the first 200 response bytes for non-2xx responses other than 401/403; the other paths expose blind status/timing/port-scan signals. /api/provider-nodes is protected by dashboard authentication by default, but dashboardGuard permits access when requireLogin=false.
flaw_origin: The lifecycle has distinct stages. 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c created the caller-controlled provider validation fetch; 0b8bed5793c7a7c9beb7a5db7368720907f61ebc added the custom-embedding response-reflection amplifier; 090886ced9a3481837f5687ec66da7d9f33eea08 applied assertPublicUrl to remote requests. The smallest commit that first wrote the advisory's specifically flawed mapped-address defense is 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5: it added only the dotted-quad /^::ffff:(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$/ match and delegation to isBlockedIpv4. Its direct parent has the guard and sink but no mapped-address branch. The exploit therefore predates this attempted fix, while the defective defense itself originates in 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5.
ai_marker: BIC commit object 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 contains the exact canonical trailer 'Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>'; author and committer are both decolua <decoluadt@example.com>. No PR-body or later-commit signal is used.
evidence: In the validated clone, `git log master -L 39,44:src/shared/utils/ssrfGuard.js` and `git log --all --reverse -S'const v4Mapped = h.match(/^::ffff:' -- src/shared/utils/ssrfGuard.js` both identify 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 as the first writer. `git show 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 -- src/shared/utils/ssrfGuard.js` shows the exact two-line addition; `git show 3a866fe18d535507f00cfd394b4f6d6e6fe2ef28:src/shared/utils/ssrfGuard.js` directly verifies that the parent lacks both lines. `git cat-file commit 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5` reproduces the parent, human author/committer, and Cursor trailer. A direct Node invocation of assertPublicUrl on master produced: http://127.0.0.1/ BLOCKED; http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/ ALLOWED with hostname [::ffff:7f00:1]; http://[::ffff:7f00:1]/ ALLOWED; and http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/ ALLOWED. Route history is reproducible with `git log --follow -- src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js`; shows of 0a28f9f924d2dc53027a910679ee3cff3e63a59c, 0b8bed5793c7a7c9beb7a5db7368720907f61ebc, and 090886ced9a3481837f5687ec66da7d9f33eea08 establish sink, disclosure, and guard integration respectively. `git tag --contains 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 --sort=version:refname` starts at v0.5.12; v0.5.8 (commit 0c47c891e7a6c1a47c35b286235a132c0a5aa0a8) predates the flawed-fix commit, while v0.5.12 (commit 90b336d9dd805b44d5b58c01dd503a9306995e75) and latest v0.5.55/master 699edac3273e13d4744bc46f6082618f08560702 contain it. The underlying unsafe route first appears in release v0.2.52 and remains vulnerable through v0.5.55. First-party issue https://github.com/decolua/9router/issues/3293 confirms the live mapped-address bypass and 200-byte disclosure. PR https://github.com/decolua/9router/pull/3370 is closed in favor of https://github.com/decolua/9router/pull/3313; PR #3313 remains OPEN and its proposed patch commit is d5277737de24aba6a297d0c0d4fdda41cd71f535. Public master still ends at 699edac3273e13d4744bc46f6082618f08560702, so no closing fix commit or patched release exists.
reasoning: The advisory is about the dead mapped-address branch, not merely the existence of a server-side fetch. BIC 8ac631d6158c0f04976a0d0f7ca9ec2b981efeb5 is the atomic first writer of that defective defense and has explicit Cursor co-authorship. However, its parent already allowed mapped IPv6 because no mapped check existed, and the route sink and response-disclosure path were written earlier. The AI-attributed commit therefore contributed security code whose claimed fix was ineffective, but it did not create the original SSRF sink or first make the attack possible. That is AI_CODE_FLAWED rather than AI_ROOT_CAUSE. The commit is a normal one-parent atomic two-line change for this flaw, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or reconstructable squash aggregate.
remaining_gap: Unpatched at audit time: the complete DNS-aware fix is only proposed in open PR #3313 (candidate commit d5277737de24aba6a297d0c0d4fdda41cd71f535), PR #3370 was closed without merge, and no fix commit or patched release is on public master; therefore fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are intentionally null.
